narrative:
The model predicts an 85% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability means the system sees strong signs that you are likely to depart soon, based on patterns from many similar employees.

The three factors that most influenced this prediction were your overall years of experience, whether you have received other job offers, and how long you have been with this current organization. These stood out as the strongest drivers compared with everything else in your profile.

Your 6–10 years of total experience pushed the prediction toward leaving. While many employees predicted to stay have only 1–5 years of experience, your mid-level tenure matches people who tend to move on rather than remain long-term. Similarly, having received other job opportunities during your time here strongly increased the likelihood of departure; most employees the model expects to stay do not receive such offers. Finally, your 1–5 years in this specific role also contributed to the “will leave” direction, as shorter current tenure often signals that someone is still evaluating their fit and may exit.

Taken together, these elements created a clear picture of someone ready to explore new horizons. The organization should discuss your career goals with you openly. You may want to reflect on what would make you want to stay, such as clearer growth paths or better rewards, before making any decisions.
